sections.h2: How does the Muhlenberg County Sheriff handle property tax bills?
sections.html:
The Muhlenberg County Sheriff's Office collects the tax, and it does so from the courthouse at 100 South Main Street in Greenville. The office keeps weekday hours from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. and answers at 270-338-3345. Mail goes to PO Box 227, Greenville, KY 42345.

  • Bills are normally mailed on October 30, and collection begins November 1.
  • The sheriff's FAQ says a bill can be paid online, but not over the phone.
  • A drop box at the back of the courthouse, by the elevator entrance, takes payments left after hours.
  • Partial payments are refused. The office requires payment in full.

The county Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) is a separate office that sets the value. Ask the PVA about the assessed amount, and ask the sheriff only about what is owed on it.

sections.h2: What is Muhlenberg County like, and how does that shape home sales?
sections.html:
Muhlenberg County covers 479 square miles of western Kentucky, of which 467 are land, and the Green River and Lake Malone are its two main waters. Greenville is the county seat and Central City is the largest city. The county was formed in 1798 from parts of Logan and Christian counties.

Coal defines the local economy and the landscape. The county held Kentucky's first commercial coal mine, opened in 1820 along the Green River at Paradise, and for most of the 1970s it produced more coal than any other county in the country. Near-surface deposits have been strip mined out, so remaining coal lies deep underground. The northern part of the county is gently rolling with river flatland and cypress swamp along Cypress Creek, while the south has higher relief, gorges and sandstone formations.

Properties therefore vary widely, from lots in Greenville and Central City to ground near Lake Malone State Park and rural parcels in former mining country. Public schools are run by one district, and since 2009 the county has had a single Muhlenberg County High School.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Muhlenberg County housing?
sections.html:
Census QuickFacts shows a slowly shrinking county with low home values, which tends to keep tax bills small. The population estimate for July 2025 is 30,634, down 1.0% from the 2020 base, and 21.3% of residents are 65 or older.

  • Housing units, 2025 estimate: 13,640. Building permits in 2025: 5.
  • Owner-occupied rate, 2020 to 2024: 78.8%.
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $127,400.
  • Median monthly owner costs: $1,167 with a mortgage, $396 without.
  • Median gross rent: $718.
  • Median household income: $51,927. About 19.1% of people live in poverty.

Roughly 88.7% of residents were in the same house a year earlier. With only 5 building permits in 2025, buyers mostly choose among existing houses.

sections.h2: Which Muhlenberg County details do buyers ask about?
sections.html:
Buyers usually ask about work, schools and commuting. On work, coal mining in the county and its neighbors began to expand again as the 2000s opened, and the Greater Muhlenberg Chamber of Commerce, formed in 2006 when the Central City and Greenville chambers merged, represents more than 155 businesses. The Census Bureau counts 537 employer establishments in the county for 2023, and total employment rose 6.7% between 2022 and 2023.

On schools, the Muhlenberg County Board of Education runs the public system, which was consolidated over the 1990s and 2000s from eight secondary schools into the one high school. On commuting, workers spend a mean of 27.0 minutes getting to their jobs. Sellers who hold a tax receipt, a recent survey if one exists and a clear deed can answer most of those questions fast, and the sheriff's receipt is the quickest proof that the year's bill is settled.

sections.h2: When are Muhlenberg County property taxes due?
sections.html:
The sheriff's posted calendar follows the statewide pattern in KRS 134.015: a 2% discount for early payment, the plain bill through December, then penalties.

Muhlenberg County Sheriff payment windows
WindowWhat you pay
November 1 to November 302% off the bill
December 1 to December 31Bill as printed
January 1 to January 315% added
February 1 to April 1521% added

Payment in full is required at every stage. A seller who owes a bill at closing should have the title company ask the sheriff for the exact figure in the window the closing falls in, because the amount changes on the first of each month during the penalty season.

sections.h2: What does waiting cost on a Muhlenberg County bill?
sections.html:
Use a $1,200 bill as an example. In November it is $1,176. In December it is $1,200. In January it is $1,260, and between February 1 and April 15 it is $1,452. Waiting through the whole season adds $276 over the November price.

The sheriff posts 21% as the single penalty for February 1 through April 15. After April 15 the county clerk takes over delinquent bills, so ask the clerk, not the sheriff, for a payoff on any year that is already past due.

sections.h2: How do I dispute a Muhlenberg County assessment?
sections.html:
Values are set as of January 1. The first step under KRS 133.120 is a conference with the Muhlenberg County PVA or a deputy, held before or during the May inspection period of the tax roll. KRS 133.045 puts that period at 13 days starting the first Monday in May, and the Department of Revenue can shift it.

If you are still unhappy, file a written appeal with the County Clerk. State the property, your reasons and your own opinion of fair cash value, and file no later than one workday after the inspection period closes. The county board of assessment appeals hears the case. Bring comparable sales, an appraisal or repair estimates, because the board denies appeals when the owner will not supply reasonable value information.

The appeal does not stop the bill from coming due. Pay tax on the value you claim, and the board's final value decides any additional amount, with interest. Skipping the county board cuts off the later appeal to the state Board of Tax Appeals.

sections.h2: Does Muhlenberg County offer a homestead exemption?
sections.html:
Yes, the statewide exemption applies to owners who are 65 or older or totally disabled. For the 2025 and 2026 assessment years the Department of Revenue sets it at $49,100, subtracted from the assessed value before tax is figured. A home assessed at the county median of $127,400 would be taxed on $78,300.

File the application with the Muhlenberg County PVA. For an age-based claim, a birth certificate, driver's license or passport proves age. A disability claim must be renewed every year unless the owner is a veteran with a service-connected disability or is classed as permanently and totally disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

sections.h2: What should a Muhlenberg County seller do about the tax bill?
sections.html:
Taxes are a personal debt of the owner on the January 1 assessment date, and a lien runs with delinquent property for up to eleven years under KRS 134.420, whoever owns the house. A buyer's title company will look for it.

  • Confirm with the sheriff that the current bill is paid, and in which window.
  • Split the year's tax in the contract so both sides know who pays what at closing.
  • Write the buyer's mailing address in the deed's in-care-of line for tax bills, which KRS 382.135 requires.
  • If the seller died, the personal representative must file an affidavit listing heirs and property values with the county clerk before closing out the estate.

faqs.q: Can I pay a Muhlenberg County tax bill by phone?
faqs.a: No. The sheriff does not take payments over the phone. You can pay online, by mail to PO Box 227 in Greenville, in person at 100 South Main Street, or in the drop box at the back of the courthouse.

faqs.q: Does Muhlenberg County accept partial property tax payments?
faqs.a: No. The sheriff's FAQ states that payment in full is required, so a partial check will not satisfy the bill.

faqs.q: When does the Muhlenberg County discount end?
faqs.a: The 2% discount runs November 1 through November 30. The plain amount is due from December 1 through December 31, and penalties start January 1.

faqs.q: What are Muhlenberg County's sheriff office hours?
faqs.a: The sheriff's office is open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. at 100 South Main Street in Greenville, and its phone is 270-338-3345.

faqs.q: Who qualifies for the homestead exemption in Muhlenberg County?
faqs.a: Owners age 65 or older, and owners classified as totally disabled, qualify. The 2025 and 2026 deduction is $49,100, and the application goes to the Muhlenberg County PVA.
